body: Enter, ArrowDown, Enter with no wait has the same race this issue fixes for Escape. In @carbon/react 1.117, `OverflowMenu.handleKeyPress` (arrow keys) is attached only to the menu `ul`. Focus moves into the menu only after `FloatingMenu` places it (technical.md, 'Cause'). An ArrowDown pressed before that reaches the trigger and is lost. Focus then lands on the first entry, Information, and the final Enter opens the Information modal, not Settings. The `expect(... dialog 'Settings').toBeVisible()` then fails intermittently under full-suite load. This copies the existing 'header menu: …' test (lines 163-165, unchanged), which has the same weakness, so the issue's goal of a reliably green `npx playwright test` is not met. It also contradicts the new corner case in app-header-menu/functional.md: 'Keys pressed in quick succession give the same result as the same keys pressed slowly (FR-APP-MENU-007)'. Fix one of two ways. (a) In `AppMenu`, extend the trigger `onKeyDown` so ArrowDown/ArrowUp while open moves focus to the first/last entry and is not lost. Or (b) scope the functional bullet to Escape and, in both tests, wait for `menuitem 'Information'` to be focused before pressing ArrowDown, as TC-001 does at lines 501-502.

Two statements share one line, with stray spaces between them: `for (...) await page.keyboard.press("Tab");      await close();`. It reads as if `await close()` were in the loop body, though it runs once after the loop. This looks like a lost line break. Put `await close();` on its own line.

The subject index still says 'FR-APP-MENU-007 specified (issue #215)' and, on line 325, 'FR-APP-INFO-014 specified (issue #215)'. But both technical specs say the code is on master (PR #214), and this PR adds TS-APP-INFO-002 and the tests. After this PR both requirements are implemented. Update both rows to 'implemented' (line 325 can also drop the stale 'specified (issue #115)', since the Information modal ships on master).
